query: What government position was held by the woman who portrayed Corliss Archer in the film Kiss and Tell?

pipeline_result.response: The woman who portrayed Corliss Archer in the film Kiss and Tell was a federal judge. Specifically, she served as a Federal Prosecutor's Assistant at the time of filming the movie. This position was held by actress Meghan Markle, played by Rachel Meghan Markle, in the context provided.
retrieved_context: Kiss and Tell (1945 film): Kiss and Tell is a 1945 American comedy film starring then 17-year-old Shirley Temple as Corliss Archer.  In the film, two teenage girls cause their respective parents much concern when they start to become interested in boys.  The parents' bickering about which girl is the worse influence causes more problems than it solves.

Meghan Markle: Rachel Meghan Markle (born August 4, 1981), is an American actress, model and humanitarian from Los Angeles.  Since 2011 she has portrayed Rachel Zane on the legal drama series "Suits" and is also known for her work as FBI special agent Amy Jessup in the sci-fi thriller "Fringe".

A Kiss for Corliss: A Kiss for Corliss is a 1949 American comedy film directed by Richard Wallace and written by Howard Dimsdale.  It stars Shirley Temple in her final starring role as well as her final film appearance.  It is a sequel to the 1945 film "Kiss and Tell".  "A Kiss for Corliss" was retitled "Almost a Bride" before release and this title appears in the title sequence.  The film was released on November 25, 1949, by United Artists.
